title: I built a prompt-to-game generation workflow — here’s what happens under the hood
author: mo-ha-tm
selftext:
I’ve been developing Topvon AI, a platform that turns natural-language prompts into playable game projects.  
One of the engineering challenges has been translating a high-level prompt into an actual game structure.  
The workflow involves:  
Interpreting the game concept and mechanics.  
Generating the project structure.  
Implementing gameplay logic.  
Handling assets and UI.  
Testing whether the generated result actually works.  
I’m currently working on improving generation reliability, especially making sure the output is playable rather than just visually convincing.  
For developers who have built procedural generation tools or game creation pipelines:  
**How do you approach validating generated gameplay logic before considering a project production-ready?**  
I’d appreciate technical feedback.
